Key bugs:

1. parse_u64 sets out=0 immediately → violates "out unchanged on failure" (e.g. "12x" or empty). Also empty string accepted (returns true, out=0) — contract says nonempty only. Overflow wraps silently (no UINT64_MAX rejection) — e.g. "18446744073...". Actually contract: rejects values above UINT64_MAX. Overflow wraps silently (no UINT64_MAX rejection) — e.g. "18446744073...". Actually contract: rejects values above UINT64_MAX. Overflow wraps silently (no UINT64_MAX rejection) — e.g. "184467440737...". Also leading zeros allowed — fine.

2. Registry::get returns string_view into names while holding lock_guard... actually returns after lock released; but vector push_back may reallocate/move strings → string_view dangles. Also add may reallocate names, invalidating earlier string_views retained by readers → dangling. Also get(i) no bounds check — out-of-bounds read for i>=size. Also get returns view to element; concurrent add may push_back causing reallocation → view dangles. Also mutex: readers retain values after get returns — but add can reallocate; no protection.
